question: A 28-year-old man presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Which set of constitutional symptoms, if present, would be documented as 'B symptoms' and significantly impact staging in Hodgkin lymphoma?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These are features of cardiac failure or superior vena cava obstruction, not lymphoma B symptoms.

answers.text: Fever >38°C, drenching night sweats, and unexplained weight loss >10% body weight in 6 months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. These are the three classic B symptoms in lymphoma (Hodgkin and NHL). Their presence changes staging from 'A' to 'B' (e.g., Stage IIA → Stage IIB) and generally indicates more aggressive disease requiring intensified therapy.
Pruritus is associated with Hodgkin lymphoma but is not a B symptom. Organomegaly reflects disease extent but is not a constitutional B symptom.
Fatigue and anorexia are general cancer symptoms but are not part of the formal B symptom criteria used in the Ann Arbor staging system.

overallFeedback.feedback: B symptoms in lymphoma are: fever >38°C, drenching night sweats, and ≥10% unexplained weight loss in the preceding 6 months. They change the Ann Arbor stage suffix from A to B.
Excellent. B symptoms (fever, night sweats, ≥10% weight loss over 6 months) are specific lymphoma staging criteria — always ask for all three when lymphoma is suspected.
